title: Live Output stalls over Tailscale + network setup is too tedious
summary: Physical iPhone/TouchDesigner test on 2026-09-08, build 058bb3da5e9665d1b06f42257642e7c3d088c92d. Observed: - Live Output reaches TouchDesigner over Tailscale, but motion delivery can pause for noticeable periods and then resume, even after switching sample rate to 30 Hz. - Current sender recreates and closes a PacketPeerUDP for every UDP JSON send and every OSC send. This is not appropriate for a sustained 10/30 Hz stream and should be replaced with persistent peers reused per endpoint, with reconnect-on-error. - Add packet sequence / monotonic timestamp so the receiver can distinguish sender stalls from packet loss. - Current network page requires typing full ws:// / http:// URLs plus repeated host/ports on an iPhone keyboard; copy/paste is awkward. - Existing live_router.json persistence should be retained and made more explicit/automatic so settings survive app restarts and normal in-place updates when the iOS app container is preserved. Planned: 1. Persistent UDP/OSC sockets in network_client.gd; recreate only when endpoint changes or a send fails. 2. Add seq + rate_hz + monotonic_ms to ioslab.live.v1 packets for diagnostics. 3. Simplify Network UI around a single destination host with generated WebSocket/HTTP endpoints and default ports/paths, instead of requiring schemes to be typed repeatedly. 4. Auto-save edits/toggles (not only on START), restore on launch, and keep backward compatibility with current saved config. 5. Keep HTTP/WS/UDP/OSC independently selectable. Do not close until a new exact-SHA IPA is physically tested against TouchDesigner and motion remains continuous.
